questions.stem: According to the passage, what activity does Marla Yoshida suggest for improving pronunciation, beyond listening and repeating?
options: Shadowing
Memorizing a dictionary
Watching movies without subtitles
Writing essays daily
questions.evidence: Yoshida suggests that they do an activity called shadowing

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that native speakers might not understand a learner even when sounds are pronounced correctly?
options: Pronouncing individual sounds correctly is enough to be understood by native speakers.
Being understood by native speakers depends on more than just correct individual sounds.
Native speakers can always understand any pronunciation.
Intonation is less important than sound pronunciation.
questions.evidence: native speakers might not understand an English learner even if the learner pronounces sounds correctly
questions.explanation_ko: 발음이 정확해도 원어민이 이해하지 못할 수 있다는 내용에서, 개별 소리의 정확한 발음만으로는 충분하지 않음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author explain the problem with the "listen and repeat" method?
options: To show why shadowing may be a more effective way to learn pronunciation
To argue that listening to English is unnecessary
To criticize teachers who use audio recordings
To explain how to make a recording
questions.evidence: The problem with listen and repeat, says Yoshida, is that when people repeat, they are often not trying to sound like the other person.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 설명은 shadowing이 왜 더 효과적인 발음 학습법일 수 있는지를 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "intonation" mean?
options: the meaning of a word
the rise and fall of the voice while speaking
the spelling of a word
the speed of speaking
questions.evidence: intonation – the up and down movement of your voice as you speak
questions.explanation_ko: intonation은 말할 때 목소리가 오르내리는 것을 뜻합니다.

questions.stem: Which choice best restates: "English sentences often emphasize words at the end of a sentence – the place where you usually find new information."
options: In English, the words at the end of a sentence are usually stressed because that is often where new information appears.
English speakers never emphasize any words in a sentence.
New information in English is usually found at the beginning of a sentence.
Emphasized words in English carry no meaning.
questions.evidence: English sentences often emphasize words at the end of a sentence – the place where you usually find new information.
questions.explanation_ko: 영어 문장은 흔히 새로운 정보가 있는 문장 끝의 단어를 강조한다는 문장을 가장 가깝게 재진술한 선택지는 첫 번째입니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 많은 영어 학습자들은 원어민의 말을 주의 깊게 듣고 문장의 오르내리는 억양을 따라 함으로써 발음을 향상시킬 수 있다.
어떤 단어를 강조할지, 즉 특별히 주의를 기울일지가 중요한 세부 사항에 포함된다.

blanks.expression: a narrow range of their voice
blanks.sentence_ko: 학습자가 목소리의 좁은 음역만 사용하면 원어민이 이해하기 어려울 수 있다.
shadowing을 한번 시도해 보시고, 어땠는지 알려 주세요!

key_points: Marla Yoshida says English learners can improve pronunciation by listening for details like pauses, emphasized words, and intonation, not just individual sounds.
Simply listening and repeating is not enough, because learners often don't focus on truly matching how the other person sounds.
English speakers use a wide range of vocal ups and downs, and learners who use a narrower range may be harder for native speakers to understand.
Yoshida recommends an activity called shadowing, in which learners listen closely and try to copy the pauses, emphasis, and intonation of a native speaker.
main_idea: Marla Yoshida recommends an activity called shadowing, which focuses on copying native speakers' pauses, emphasis, and intonation rather than just individual sounds, to improve pronunciation.
restate_sentence: Native speakers also communicate by using pauses, and by saying some words more forcefully than others.
